new_service_wizard.help.service_id.short: Unique code, max. 20 characters (recommended: prefix + digits)
new_service_wizard.help.service_id.long: Stable identifier of the service. Recommended convention: a 3–4 letter prefix plus a numeric code, e.g. WPS001 = Workplace Services #001. The code never changes and is used in reports, imports and URLs.
new_service_wizard.help.title.short: Full name that users understand — no abbreviations
new_service_wizard.help.title.long: The name should be clear to the consumer, not to the implementation team. Describe the value the service delivers, not how it is built. Example: "Corporate mobile devices" instead of "MDM Provisioning".
new_service_wizard.help.service_type.sho: Category from the internal service type taxonomy
new_service_wizard.help.service_type.lon: The service type defines the nature of delivery. CF = Core Function (primary IT services), EF = Enabling Function (supporting services), EP = External Provider (third party). Correct classification is key for portfolio management and reporting.
Current lifecycle stage — controls visibility in the catalogue
Service lifecycle: Draft, Live (published), Deprecated or Retired. Reviews and approvals are handled separately in the governance workflow.
new_service_wizard.help.summary.short: Short description shown in the catalogue — 1–2 sentences
new_service_wizard.help.summary.long: The summary is the first thing a consumer sees in the catalogue. Write from their point of view: what they get and how it helps them. Recommended length: 1–2 sentences, max. 200 characters. Avoid technical jargon.
new_service_wizard.help.consumer_value.s: The concrete value or benefit the consumer gets
new_service_wizard.help.consumer_value.l: Describe the concrete outcome or benefit for the consumer. Example: "Access to email and calendar from any device, reliable operation with a 99.9% SLA and secure encryption."
new_service_wizard.help.requestable.shor: Can consumers request this service from the catalogue?
new_service_wizard.help.requestable.long: Turn this on only when there is a clear channel through which consumers request the service. When it is off, the service is informational only or is assigned outside the catalogue.
new_service_wizard.help.request_channel_: Choose the entry point for requesting the service. Example channels: ITSM portal, email, self-service portal, Teams or phone.
Direct link to the request portal or form

Direct URL of the portal or form through which consumers submit requests. It shortens the consumer journey — from the service detail they can go straight to the request without searching for the right place.
new_service_wizard.help.approval_require: Does the request need approval before fulfilment?

Some services require formal approval before fulfilment — budget authorisation, a security review or manager consent. When enabled, the request goes through an approval workflow before delivery starts.
new_service_wizard.help.fulfillment_lead: Expected time from request to delivery
State a realistic delivery time including any approval. Examples: "Same business day", "1–2 business days", "2–4 weeks (including approval)". Consumers see this time in the catalogue.
new_service_wizard.help.target_audience_: Who the service is for — the eligible user group
Describe the eligible consumer group so users can tell at once whether they are entitled to the service. Examples: "All employees", "IT staff only", "Project managers in approved cost centres".
new_service_wizard.help.portfolio_group_: The portfolio the service belongs to — for governance and reporting

Services are grouped into portfolios for governance, budgeting and reporting. The portfolio group determines the ownership chain, budget allocation and which portfolio review board manages the service.
new_service_wizard.help.service_line_cod: Service line that groups related services
A service line is a logical grouping of related services under shared operational and financial management. It helps compare cost and capacity across services of a similar nature.
new_service_wizard.help.organizational_e: Unit or team responsible for operation and funding
The organisational element identifies the unit (department, team, business unit) responsible for funding and operating the service. It is used for charge-back/show-back reporting and governance.
new_service_wizard.help.global_service_g: The global service group brings together services across portfolios for reporting, comparison and strategic assessment. Fill it in only if your organisation actually uses this view.
new_service_wizard.help.security_classif: Highest sensitivity level of data processed by the service

Indicates the highest sensitivity level of data the service processes. It is used for access control, compliance reporting and consumer eligibility. It follows the internal classification scheme (ISO 27001 or NIST).
new_service_wizard.help.service_owner.sh: The person accountable for the service end to end
new_service_wizard.help.service_owner.lo: The service owner is accountable for the service end to end, represents it in governance forums and approves significant changes. This field is shown in the service detail.
new_service_wizard.help.service_owner_em: Service owner email — consumers can use it to get in touch

The service owner email is shown in the service detail as the contact for escalations or questions about the service definition. It differs from the support contact — the service owner is responsible for strategy, not operations.
new_service_wizard.help.vlastnik.short: Area owner — accountable for the portfolio or domain
new_service_wizard.help.vlastnik.long: The area owner is accountable for a group of related services or a whole domain. They keep the portfolio aligned and are the contact for senior business stakeholders.
new_service_wizard.help.manager.short: Delivery manager — responsible for operational delivery
new_service_wizard.help.manager.long: The service delivery manager coordinates day-to-day operation, SLA fulfilment and escalations. Unlike the service owner (strategy), the delivery manager handles operational issues and communication with resolver groups.
new_service_wizard.help.sla_availability: Target uptime in % (e.g. 99.9 = max. 8.7 h downtime per year)

SLA availability defines the percentage of time the service must be operational. 99.9% = max. 8.7 h/year downtime; 99.5% = max. 43.8 h/year. Choose a realistic target that matches actual infrastructure capacity, not an aspiration.
new_service_wizard.help.domains.short: Network domains / zones where the service is available
new_service_wizard.help.domains.long: Network domains represent physical or logical availability zones. The mapping tells consumers where they can use the service from. Services in several domains may have different endpoints or support contacts per domain.
new_service_wizard.help.c3_mapping.short: Optional — map the service to the C3 capability taxonomy
new_service_wizard.help.c3_mapping.long: The C3 taxonomy maps IT services to capabilities. Mapping enables capability coverage reporting, gap analysis and portfolio rationalisation. Full mapping is available in the editor after the service is created.
